clue.text: Spectacles in fair ground? There’s singing about it

indicators.note: something ground has been crushed and broken up, so the letters are reduced and remixed
to be about something is to surround it, so one piece goes round the other

blocks.note: vocals are the sung parts of a song
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone at a fairground notices glasses while a singalong goes on around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fair ground' looks like one word, fairground, but splits into fodder and signal; 'it' points back to that rearranged fair, which sits inside VOCALS after the V.
explanation.definitionFit: Varifocals are eyeglasses whose lenses change power gradually from top to bottom, a kind of spectacles.

clue.text: Clothing store’s clothing filling the box up

indicators.note: clothing is what covers the outside, so only the outer letters of the word are kept
filling something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes into another
in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

blocks.note: the box is British slang for the television
the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A clothes shop's stock is packed into a box ready to be shipped.
explanation.walkthrough: Both uses of 'clothing' mislead: the first is the definition, the second means the outside of a word. 'The box' is British slang for television; the whole assembly is then read upward.
explanation.definitionFit: A vest is an item of clothing, an undershirt in Britain or a waistcoat in America.

clue.text: Terrorise legless reveller

indicators.note: legless is British slang for very drunk, and a drunk word staggers into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, every letter rearranged

explanation.surface: A drunken partygoer frightens everyone around them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Legless' reads as describing the reveller, which suits the picture, but it is the signal to rearrange 'Terrorise'.
explanation.definitionFit: A roisterer is someone who celebrates noisily and boisterously, the same as a reveller.

clue.text: Receiving poor remuneration, lumberjack’s work generates sympathy

indicators.note: whatever receives something takes it in, so one piece is placed inside the other

blocks.note: lumberjacks cut down trees, which is felling
poor pay is a low fee

explanation.surface: Underpaid lumberjacks earn the public's sympathy for their hard work.
explanation.walkthrough: The opening phrase looks like a description of the lumberjack's pay, but it is wordplay to be enclosed, and 'generates' merely joins the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Fellow feeling is a shared sense of understanding with another person, essentially a synonym for sympathy.

clue.text: Crooked cheat smuggling too many drugs in part of cell?

indicators.note: crooked means bent out of shape, so the letters are twisted into another order
smuggling something means hiding it inside, so one piece is concealed within the other

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
OD is short for overdose, taking too much of a drug

explanation.surface: A dishonest crook hides a stash of drugs inside a prison cell.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface makes 'cell' a prison cell; the question mark warns that it is an electric cell, a battery.
explanation.definitionFit: A cathode is one of the two electrodes of an electrical battery cell, so it is a component of one.

clue.text: Endlessly slow Parisian is fatter than the others

indicators.note: without an end means the final letter is cut off

blocks.note: largo is the musical direction for a slow tempo, here losing its last letter
est is French for 'is'

explanation.surface: A sluggish Parisian is the stoutest person in the group.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Slow' is a tempo marking, largo, not the adjective it appears to be; 'Parisian' tells you to put 'is' into French.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of large describes something bigger or broader than every other one in a group.

clue.text: Book with e.g. poetry kid associated with Homer

blocks.note: B is a standard abbreviation for book
poetry is one example of an art

explanation.surface: A volume of poetry for children linked with the ancient poet Homer.
explanation.walkthrough: Homer suggests the Greek epic poet, which fits 'poetry', but this Homer is Homer Simpson of the cartoon.
explanation.definitionFit: Bart Simpson is the son of Homer Simpson in the animated sitcom The Simpsons.

clue.text: Story in vacuous action or sci-fi film

indicators.note: vacuous means empty, so the word is emptied of its middle and only the outer letters remain
being in something means sitting inside it, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: a story can be a falsehood, a lie
first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: A mindless action movie or a science fiction film with a thin plot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Story' here means a fib, not a plot, and it sits inside the emptied 'action'.
explanation.definitionFit: Alien is Ridley Scott's 1979 science fiction horror movie, so the title is an example of one.

clue.text: Hot after moving around carefully

indicators.note: once letters have been moving they no longer stand in their original places

blocks.note: taken as written, then rearranged
around a number means approximately, roughly

explanation.surface: Feeling overheated after carefully shifting things about.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Around' looks like part of the moving, but it is a synonym for approximately, placed after the rearranged 'Hot'.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something thoroughly means doing it with complete care and attention to detail, a close synonym.

clue.text: Son is going to drink heartily

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for son
'will' expresses the future, like 'is going to'

explanation.surface: A boy announces that he is about to start drinking enthusiastically.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is going to' reads as a plain future tense joining the parts, but it is itself the auxiliary verb that supplies the second piece.
explanation.definitionFit: To swill is to gulp drink greedily and in large quantities, matching hearty drinking.

clue.text: Hollywood celeb not in shot after parting remark

indicators.note: something shot is ruined or wrecked, so the letters are broken and reassembled
coming after places this piece behind the other in the answer

blocks.note: ta-ra is an informal British way of saying goodbye
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A film star leaves a scene without appearing on camera, saying goodbye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shot' suggests a film take, fitting the Hollywood picture, but it signals the rearrangement of 'not in'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quentin Tarantino is a famous American film director, a well-known figure in the movie industry.

clue.text: Fiancé follows sister accepting work that isn’t supposed to amuse

indicators.note: accepting something means taking it in, so one piece goes inside another
following means coming behind, so this piece is placed second

blocks.note: a nun is a religious sister
op is short for opus, a musical work
one's intended is the person one plans to marry

explanation.surface: A man engaged to a woman trails after her sister, who has taken a job that is no fun.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase describing a remark; the answer is what people say after an accidental wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Said after an unintentional play on words, the phrase disclaims any attempt at humour in the previous remark.

clue.text: Twain book about sailor on whiskey

indicators.note: in an across clue, being on something means coming after it
being about something means going round it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: a tome is a large book
Whiskey is the NATO phonetic alphabet word for W
OS stands for ordinary seaman

explanation.surface: A Mark Twain novel about a seafarer who drinks whiskey.
explanation.walkthrough: Twain looks like the author Mark Twain, but it is the old word for two. Whiskey is a NATO alphabet letter, and the sailor is an ordinary seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: Twain is an archaic word for two, and a twosome is a pair of people or things.

clue.text: Stage entertainment long before debut of opera

indicators.note: a debut is a first appearance, so only the initial letter is kept
coming before places this piece first in the answer

blocks.note: to long for something is to pant for it
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A show that ran for a long time before the opera premiered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective about time but is the verb, to yearn. Panto is a British family Christmas show with comic songs and cross-dressing.
explanation.definitionFit: Pantomime is a traditional British theatrical show staged around Christmas, a form of stage entertainment.

clue.text: Maybe twenty winks before noon, or fewer than that?

definitions.note: the definition describes the answer as a number smaller than twenty

indicators.note: coming before places this piece first in the answer

blocks.note: forty winks is a short nap, so twenty winks is half of one
N is an abbreviation for noon

explanation.surface: A brief morning nap, or perhaps even shorter than that.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Twenty' reads as part of the nap, but the definition makes it a number: six is fewer than twenty. Forty winks is an idiom for a nap.
explanation.definitionFit: Half a dozen is six, a quantity smaller than the twenty mentioned earlier in the clue.

clue.text: Somewhat disheartened accountant getting sack

indicators.note: losing the heart removes everything in the middle, leaving only the ends

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
to sack a place is to plunder it, to rifle it

explanation.surface: An accountant is a little dispirited at being fired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Disheartened' and 'sack' paint a dismissal, but 'sack' means plunder, and 'Somewhat' moves from describing the mood to being the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is used adverbially to mean slightly or to a small degree, just like somewhat.

clue.text: Support for guy, figure with back in torment and leg

indicators.note: the back of a word is its end, so just the final letter is kept

blocks.note: ten is a number, a figure
the last letter of the word
peg is informal for a leg

explanation.surface: Someone with back pain and a bad leg needs help to support a man.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Guy' reads as a man, but it is a guy rope, which holds a tent steady and is anchored by a peg.
explanation.definitionFit: A guy rope is fastened to the ground by a tent peg, which holds it taut and supports it.

clue.text: Minister has this drink, needing loo if bursting

indicators.note: something bursting breaks apart, so these letters scatter and regroup

blocks.note: port is a fortified wine
taken as written, then rearranged

explanation.surface: A government minister drinks this and then desperately needs a toilet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'If' looks like a conjunction but is fodder alongside 'loo', a British word for toilet; 'bursting' signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: A government minister holds a portfolio, the area of responsibility such as health or defence.

clue.text: Agitation of whistleblower turning workers tense

indicators.note: turning round makes the letters face the opposite way

blocks.note: a referee blows the whistle in a match
workers are often men in crosswords
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: A whistleblower causes unrest by making the staff anxious.
explanation.walkthrough: A whistleblower is surface-wise someone exposing wrongdoing, but here it is a referee; 'tense' looks like an adjective for the workers but supplies a letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Ferment, as a noun, means a state of unrest or excitement, a close synonym for agitation.

clue.text: More corpulent bishop I introduced to King Edward?

indicators.note: introducing something to another means inserting it into it

blocks.note: King Edward is a British potato variety, and a potato is a tuber
B is the chess notation for bishop
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rather stout bishop is presented to a king.
explanation.walkthrough: King Edward looks like a monarch, but the question mark hints at the potato variety popular in Britain, which is a kind of tuber.
explanation.definitionFit: Tubby means short and fat, so tubbier is the comparative meaning fatter or plumper.

clue.text: Nurse hands round peeled fig or bit of grape plant, say

indicators.note: peeling strips the outer layer, so only the inner letter is kept
going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: to nurse is to tend or care for
right and left hands, R and L
the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: A nurse passes round some skinned figs or grapes on a plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hands' looks like a verb, passing round, but it is a noun giving two letters for right and left.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendril is the thin coiling shoot a climbing plant such as a vine uses to cling, so it is one part.

clue.text: Show audacity — hear setter put on weight

indicators.note: in a down clue, what is put on something sits above it, coming earlier

blocks.note: a judge hears a case, which means trying it
the setter refers to themselves as I
a ton is a unit of weight

explanation.surface: An audacious remark: listen, the puzzle compiler has gained weight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hear' seems to invite listening, but it is the legal sense of hearing a case. 'Try it on' is British slang for chancing your luck.
explanation.definitionFit: To try it on is a British idiom for attempting something cheeky to see if you can get away with it.

clue.text: Copper seizing stolen garment from Asia

indicators.note: seizing something means grabbing hold of it, enclosing it

blocks.note: a copper is a police officer, here a Detective Inspector
hot is slang for stolen goods

explanation.surface: A police officer confiscates a stolen item of clothing brought from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: Copper suggests the metal Cu, but here it is a policeman, who supplies the outer letters of a detective rank.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is a loincloth worn by men in India, an item of South Asian clothing.

clue.text: Repeatedly running round Italy? It might make you cry

indicators.note: going round something means surrounding it

blocks.note: a machine that is running is on, given twice
I is the international car code for Italy

explanation.surface: Running laps around Italy over and over would bring anyone to tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Running' looks like jogging but means switched on, written twice with Italy between.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting an onion releases a chemical irritant that makes the eyes water, as though weeping.

clue.text: Spooner’s put red meat in herbal seasoning

indicators.note: Reverend Spooner famously swapped the opening sounds of words

blocks.note: to put something down is to lay it; its opening sound is traded with the next word's
beef is red meat; its opening sound is traded with the previous word's

explanation.surface: A cook places red meat in a herb rub.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the initial L and B sounds of the two words gives the herb.
explanation.definitionFit: Bay leaves are aromatic leaves of the laurel tree, used dried to flavour stews and soups.

clue.text: Letters from abroad satisfy revolutionary

indicators.note: a revolution turns something right round, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: to sate is to satisfy fully

explanation.surface: Mail from overseas pleases a political radical.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters from abroad' suggests foreign correspondence, but means letters of a foreign alphabet.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet, so etas are characters from a foreign script.

clue.text: Relish drinking vermouth, case of grenadine and one German spirit

indicators.note: a case is the outside covering, so just the outer letters are kept
drinking takes something inside, so one piece is swallowed by another

blocks.note: relish and zest both mean enthusiasm or gusto
It is short for Italian vermouth, as in gin and It
first and last letters of the word
the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Enjoying a cocktail of vermouth, grenadine and German schnapps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'German spirit' reads as schnapps in a drinks list, but it is the definition, a literal translation of a German word.
explanation.definitionFit: Zeitgeist is a German word meaning the spirit of the times, the defining mood of an era.

clue.text: Artful when packaging large pottery

indicators.note: packaging something wraps it up, putting it inside

blocks.note: artful and deft both mean skilful
L is the clothing-size abbreviation for large

explanation.surface: Being skilful when wrapping big ceramic pieces for shipping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artful' suggests cunning, but here it means deft, which wraps around the letter for large.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is blue and white glazed earthenware made in the Dutch town of Delft.

clue.text: Muses, perhaps, during meditation in east

indicators.note: something occurring during a period sits within it, so the letters lie inside the phrase

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of one word, the next, and the start of the last

explanation.surface: Someone ponders while meditating somewhere in the East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Muses' looks like a verb, ponders, but it is a noun: the Muses of Greek myth, who were nine in number.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek mythology there were nine Muses, so the number describes them, and the 'perhaps' marks an example.

clue.text: What Jim Morrison did entrances

blocks.note: the singer led the rock band the Doors as its frontman
the main ways into houses at the street side

explanation.walkthrough: 'Entrances' could be a verb, enchants, which suits a rock star, but it is the noun for ways in.
explanation.definitionFit: Main ways into buildings are front doors, while to front a band means to be its lead singer.
